items.title: Comparing Offertory Melodies of Five Medieval Christian Chant Traditions
items.who: P. van Kranenburg and G. Maessen
items.note: Applies computational melodic comparison to offertories shared across five Latin chant traditions, including the Old Roman and Gregorian versions.

items.title: The Earliest Antiphons of the Roman Office
items.venue: Chant, Liturgy, and the Inheritance of Rome (Boydell)
items.note: Uses Old Roman and Gregorian Office antiphons comparatively to identify the oldest layer of the Roman Office, in a volume of essays honouring Joseph Dyer.

items.title: Writing Sounds in Carolingian Europe: The Invention of Musical Notation
items.note: Reconstructs the ninth-century emergence of neume notation, constraining when Frankish melodies could first have been fixed in writing.

items.title: Studying Large Plainchant Corpora Using chant21
items.who: B. Cornelissen, W. Zuidema and J. A. Burgoyne
items.note: Python library for parsing Cantus volpiano and GABC chant encodings into music21, making corpus-scale melodic analysis practicable.

items.title: Renewal, Heritage, and Exchange in Eleventh-Century Roman Chant Traditions
items.venue: Urban Developments in Late Antique and Medieval Rome (Amsterdam UP)
items.note: Examines the eleventh-century Roman chant books, the period when Old Roman melodies were first written down, as products of local renewal and exchange.

items.title: Revisiting 'Toledo, Rome, and the Legacy of Gaul': new evidence from the Divine Office
items.note: Identifies nearly two dozen Franco-Roman responsories shared with the Old Hispanic rite, extending Levy's case for non-Roman material in the Gregorian repertory.

items.title: ChantLab and Genome of Melody code repositories
items.who: Genome of Melody project (J. Hajič jr et al.)
items.note: Open code for aligning volpiano chant melodies and running MrBayes phylogenetic analyses, released alongside the group's chant phylogeny papers.

items.title: Gregorian melody, modality, and memory: Segmenting chant with Bayesian nonparametrics
items.who: V. Lanz and J. Hajič jr
items.note: Tests the centonisation idea that chant is built from reusable melodic segments, relevant to separating formulaic convergence from shared descent.

items.title: Genome of melody: applying bioinformatics to study the evolution of Gregorian chant
items.who: J. Hajič jr, V. Lanz and G. A. Ballen
items.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
items.note: Shows that phylogenetic models on aligned melodies recover historically plausible patterns among Gregorian sources; Old Roman sources are not included.

items.title: A variánsalkotás mintázatai órómai és gregorián kéziratokban (Patterns of variants in Old Roman and Gregorian chant manuscripts)
items.note: Applies digital stemmatics and descriptive statistics to melodic variants in the Old Roman sources, read against their Gregorian analogues, to infer sub-traditions among the Roman books.

items.title: Making Chant Computing Easy: CantusCorpus v1.0 and the PyCantus Library
items.who: A. Dvořáková, T. Eipert, D. Lacoste and J. Hajič jr
items.venue: Transactions of the International Society for Music Information Retrieval
items.note: Releases a single dataset combining the Cantus Database and allied Cantus Index databases (nearly 900,000 chants in over 2,000 sources) with a Python library.

items.title: What did the dove sing to Pope Gregory? Ancestral melody reconstruction in Gregorian chant using Bayesian phylogenetics
items.who: G. A. Ballen, K. H. Mühlová and J. Hajič jr
items.note: Reconstructs ancestral melodies on a time-calibrated tree of fourteen sources and proposes encoding Old Roman sources to test their chronology against Gregorian.

items.title: Towards a foundational model for recognising diastematic Gregorian notation
items.who: D. Kurek and J. Hajič jr
items.note: Unifies four optical music recognition datasets for pitched chant notation in one encoding and trains a shared model, a route to transcribing pitched sources at scale.
